label: Mudafara
note: Stretched in boiled water but kept in brine like a feta.

about.text: A Sudanese stretched-curd cheese: rennet-set cow's milk curd is scalded in hot water, pulled into threads, braided and stored in brine.

links.name: FAO, The technology of traditional milk products in developing countries, ch. 7

how.label: stretch, braid
how.text: The curd is scalded and stretched into threads, then plaited. It is pickled in brine rather than ripened dry. Plant coagulants (Solanum dubium, S. torvum) have also been tried for white and mudaffara cheese.

links.name: FAO, The technology of traditional milk products in developing countries, ch. 7

steps.note: With rennet tablets; the braided type is set at 30–40 °C for about 5 h.
No culture is added; the acidity comes from the milk's own flora.

steps.name: stretch
steps.note: In boiled water, the curd heated close to its melting point.

facts.v: Whole cow; braided cheese also goat or sheep
Drained curd mixed with 10–15 % salt and black cumin (Nigella), warmed, cut into 5 × 15 cm strips and plaited; packed in 10–15 kg tins of brine
